stem: A child has a fracture that tends to drift back into deformity after initial reduction; which plastering principle best addresses this problem?

options.text: Use traction for all distal injuries
Leave the reduction unmaintained until review
Trap the fingers to stop movement
Always choose a broad arm sling

explanation: Counteract deforming forces is the principle that best prevents a reduced fracture from redisplacing in plaster.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Immobilisation must maintain the reduction by opposing the forces that would otherwise pull the fracture back into deformity.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because plaster should oppose the deforming forces that would otherwise redisplace the fracture.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because traction is not used for all distal injuries and does not directly describe the plastering principle asked about.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the reduction should be maintained, not left unprotected until review.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because fingers should not be trapped in the cast.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a broad arm sling may be useful in some injuries, but it is not the core principle for preventing redisplacement.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
